title: ‘‘KINGDOMNOMICS’’ (PART 2)
mv: The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the LORD of hosts.
mvp: “The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the LORD of hosts.” Haggai 2:8
assignment: Mention five (5) people in the Bible who gathered wealth by vanity with a scriptural reference each (2x5=10 marks).

b.x: In this lesson, we shall consider the biblical position on the basic factors of production. This will serve as a guide on what our disposition should be towards them.

In a literary sense, land is regarded as soil. However, in economics, land refers to a natural resource that can be utilised to produce income. God owns all lands as well as the materials and the forces which nature gives freely for man’s aid, in land, such as, water, air, light and heat (Psalm 24:1). God gives land to man to explore and possess (Genesis 13:14-17; Psalm115:16). Believers need to ask God for the appropriate location to dwell or do business (Genesis 12:1; Genesis 26:2, 12). Land must be put into profitable use because it is available in limited quantity. (Proverbs 12:11) Appreciate God for making the land fruitful (Psalm 67:5-6). No land is barren; every land is created for a purpose (mining, agriculture, tourism, and so on). We are to explore and maximise the use of the land (2 Kings 2:21).

Labour is another important factor of production. It involves human services and efforts for the production of goods or services. In economic terms, work, physical or mental, carried out for monetary purposes, is called labour. God wants man to work (Genesis 2:15; 1 Thessalonians 4:11). God promises sweet sleep and rest for a labouring man (Ecclesiastes 5:12; Matthew 11:28). In all labour, there is profit (Proverbs 13:11; Ephesians 4:28). The labour of the righteous adds value to lives, (Proverbs 10:16) and there shall be no labour loss (Isaiah 62:8). When we plant, we shall eat of the fruit thereof and when we build, we shall inhabit (Psalm128:2; Isaiah 65:21-23). Believers must not rule out God in their endeavours because only God crowns labour with success (Psalm 127:1). Above all, believers should labour to inherit the kingdom of God (John 6:27).

In this context, capital refers to money used for income creation purposes. God owns the gold, silver and every resource that can be converted to money (Haggai 2:8; Psalm 50:10). Money is good. Ecclesiastes 10:19 says, money answers all things, and it is a defence (Ecclesiastes 7:12). However, believers should avoid excessive pursuit of money (Proverbs 13:11; 1Timothy 6:10). Money should not be spent anyhow; there must be a plan (Luke 14:28-30). In kingdom economics, believers should put God first (Matthew 6:33) in their pursuit of money and acquire it legitimately. Remember, you cannot serve God and mammon (Matthew 6:24).

An individual who creates an enterprise is called an entrepreneur. A child of God is expected to be a creator/innovator of good things, which include viable business endeavours (Ephesians 2:10). He/she should equally be able to maximise the use of all other factors of production. A believer is expected to pay his or her workers as at when due (Deuteronomy 24:14-15; 1 Timothy 5:18). Believers should not be dubious in their dealings (Proverbs 28:8; James 5:4), for it is the blessing of God that enriches (Proverbs 10:22). An entrepreneur needs to be focused and adapt to changes in the national economy, industries and markets (Acts 16:14a).
God owns all factors of production (Psalm 24:1). Put Him first in all your endeavours and you will be profitable on earth and lay up treasures in Heaven.

i: Differentiate between land and labour in kingdom economics.
Explain capital and entrepreneur as factors of production.
